conversions.shown_step:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={5}^{u},\,u={x}^{3}+1.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={5}^{u}\ln(5),\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={5}^{u}\ln(5)\cdot (3{x}^{2}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\ln(5)\cdot {5}^{u} \\  & =3{x}^{2}\ln(5)\cdot {5}^{{x}^{3}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$
